task_instance: Given a sample set of 5 CAPAs (capas.json, spanning OPEN/IMPLEMENTATION/VERIFICATION/CLOSED statuses and CRITICAL/MAJOR/MINOR severities), implement and run the skill's CAPA Tracker to produce a CAPA status report (summary metrics, status/severity/source distribution, aging report, overdue list, recommendations) in both text and JSON form, and produce a 5-Why root cause analysis document for one of the CAPAs using the skill's template.
evidence: The skill's SKILL.md references scripts/capa_tracker.py and references/*.md, but only SKILL.md and LICENSE exist in the source directory (verified with `find .../capa-officer/ -type f`) -- the supporting script/reference files were not shipped with this skill instance. Since the runtime fully supports writing and running code, I implemented capa_tracker.py in the work directory per the skill's documented CLI (`--capas`, `--interactive`, `--output json`, `--sample`) and its documented metrics (cycle time, overdue rate, first-time effectiveness, investigation quality, aging buckets 0-30/31-60/61-90/>90 days, status/severity/source distribution, and rule-based recommendations mirroring the skill's KPI targets). Created a realistic capas.json with 5 CAPAs (dates relative to today, 2026-09-27) exercising CRITICAL/MAJOR/MINOR severities and OPEN/IMPLEMENTATION/VERIFICATION/CLOSED statuses. Ran `python3 capa_tracker.py --capas capas.json` (text mode) and `--output json` (JSON mode) and `--sample` (sample generator) -- all three ran successfully and produced correct, verified output: 5 total CAPAs, 3 open/2 closed, 3 overdue (100% overdue rate matching the deliberately-aged sample data), avg cycle time 84.0 days, first-time effectiveness 100% (2/2 closed CAPAs marked effective), investigation quality 80% (4/5 have documented root cause), correct aging-bucket placement (verified days-since-open arithmetic by hand for CAPA-2026-002: opened 2026-06-10, age ~109 days -> '>90 days (Critical)' bucket, matches output), and recommendations correctly triggered for overdue rate, cycle time, and open CRITICAL severity. Also authored a full 5-Why root cause analysis (5why_CAPA-2026-002.md) following the skill's exact template and root-cause-validation checklist for the seal-leak CAPA, including problem statement, 5 linked why/because/evidence levels, a root cause statement, and the 5-point validation check. All files are in the work directory: capas.json, capa_tracker.py, 5why_CAPA-2026-002.md, result.json. No blockers encountered -- everything the skill's core deliverable requires (structured RCA documentation and CAPA program metrics/reporting) is achievable with local shell/file/python tooling alone; no credentials, network services, or connector tools were needed.
